sources.entry: Your first 90 days as CTO or VP Engineering - Will Larson

summary.title: Your first 90 days as CTO or VP Engineering.
summary.one_liner: A tactical playbook for a new CTO or VP of Engineering covering priorities, listening tours, support networks, organizational process, hiring, execution, and technology decisions during the first ninety days.
takeaways: Start by understanding the business, culture, and team before changing systems; avoid rushing to make changes.
Set explicit priorities (business, culture, stakeholders, execution, technical quality, inclusion, sustainable pace) and measurable goals for each.
Build trust through listening tours, recurring one-on-ones and skip-levels, shadowing support tickets and customer meetings, and sharing weekly observations.
Limit organizational changes to one or two at a time, and limit hiring to three or fewer key missing roles.
Avoid having too many lightly held technology opinions and avoid judging past decisions without their historical context.
summary.summary: Will Larson's article, an unedited chapter from O'Reilly's The Engineering Executive's Primer, gives tactical recommendations for someone starting as a CTO or VP of Engineering. It first defines the role broadly (executive team member, responsible for technical execution and engineering people management) and proposes a set of priority areas with measurable goals. The rest is organized into sections on learning and trust, support systems, organizational health, hiring, execution, and technology, each with concrete actions and common anti-patterns. It also cites a reading list including The First 90 Days, The Manager's Path, and Peopleware.
